evaluations.evidence: create a new game
evaluations.rationale: Creating a game is a foundational capability and does not inherently require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators to a game inherently depends on a game existing to invite them to.

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item
evaluations.rationale: Starting a round implies an existing game context in which the round occurs.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Seeing items for a session depends on items having been created/added for that session.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item inherently requires that a list of items already exists.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding an item to a list presupposes an existing game/session context in which that list exists.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item inherently depends on items already existing.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item inherently depends on items already existing.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Showing estimates presupposes that estimates can be given in a round/game.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting an average inherently depends on estimates having been collected.

evaluations.evidence: filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Auto-filling based on all estimators' cards depends on the ability for estimators to submit/show cards (estimates).

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering an agreed estimate presupposes an estimation round with collected estimates for an item.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating inherently depends on having previously estimated items in the same session.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing stories implies a destination context (a game/session backlog) into which stories are imported.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/pasting stories implies a destination context (a game/session backlog) into which stories are added.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games inherently depends on games having been created/stored previously.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a transcript depends on a game existing (and having recorded content) to view.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript depends on the ability to view/access a transcript of a game.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript depends on the ability to view/access a transcript of a game.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game inherently depends on games existing to delete.

evaluations.evidence: create an account for the application
evaluations.rationale: Account creation is self-contained and does not inherently require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Logging in inherently depends on accounts existing to authenticate against.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Changing account details inherently depends on an account existing (and typically being able to access it).

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an account inherently depends on an account existing.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Timezone display is a cross-cutting presentation requirement and does not inherently depend on another specific story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminders inherently depend on accounts existing (with stored email addresses/credentials).

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Card-set selection is a configurable rule and can be implemented without requiring another specific story as a prerequisite.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators (with a limit) depends on the base capability to invite estimators to a game.

evaluations.evidence: join a game ... on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining a game via a received URL depends on the game being created and the invitation/URL being provided.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Seeing the item being estimated depends on an item having been created/selected for the round.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Seeing all items for the session depends on items having been created/added for that session.

evaluations.evidence: see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: This depends on estimators being able to join and submit estimates in a game/round.

evaluations.evidence: shown all estimates ... after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Showing all estimates after everyone has estimated depends on the ability for estimators to submit estimates and be tracked.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until ... all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate depends on the existence of an estimation mechanism and the reveal/show behavior.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Prior estimates can only exist if estimates have been made and stored for the story/rounds.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: This depends on estimates being submitted and associated with estimators in a round.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: A shared timer feature can be implemented as a standalone capability without inherently requiring another specific story as a prerequisite.

evaluations.evidence: timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Resetting based on all participants playing an estimate depends on the timer feature and on the estimation/reveal flow being present.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Scrolling through prior rounds depends on rounds having occurred and their stories/estimates being recorded.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Consistent card ordering is a self-contained UI/behavior rule and does not inherently require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate depends on an estimation/draw mechanism existing and tracking completion state.

evaluations.evidence: thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a thumbnail photo is a self-contained profile/UI enhancement and does not inherently require another specific story as a prerequisite.

evaluations.evidence: site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance is a cross-cutting quality requirement and does not inherently depend on another story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: A glossary can be created independently of other functional stories.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Database indexing is an internal optimization task that can be performed without requiring another specific story as a prerequisite.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Cross-browser compatibility is a cross-cutting quality requirement and does not inherently depend on another story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is cross-cutting and not inherently dependent on another specific story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance responsiveness is a cross-cutting quality requirement and does not inherently depend on another story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is a cross-cutting capability and does not inherently depend on another story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design is a cross-cutting requirement and does not inherently depend on another story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Error pages can be implemented independently as a general system behavior without requiring another specific story first.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Storing results (even anonymized) depends on the existence of results/estimates being produced and stored by the game.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Usage metrics inherently depend on the game being used and usage data being generated/recorded.
